_how_to_use: PASTE ONLY THE `prompt` FIELD INTO THE IMAGE MODEL. Nothing else in this file is for the model. Pasting the whole file produced a collage of several captioned slides, because `renditions_wanted` lists two sizes, `framing.aspect_ratios` lists two ratios, and headline_in_app / caption_in_app are text - the model read all of that as a brief to draw multiple frames with words on them. Those fields are for the render pipeline and for whoever writes the app copy.
_source_image_note: Save the image you keep in this folder named `03_welcome_3_library_stays_yours` with whatever extension the model gave you - .jpg, .png, .jpeg and .webp are all accepted. Only the NAME has to match this file; the extension does not. lessons/scripts/tutor_images.py then renders it to renders/03_welcome_3_library_stays_yours/ as slide_1080x1920 (9:16 phone slide) and card_1080x1350 (4:5). Renditions are always written as PNG regardless of the source format.
audience: a parent or guardian setting up for a learner
caption_in_app: Every lesson you attend is saved to rewatch any time - even between subscriptions.
intent: a parent seeing accumulated value - the work is done and it stays done, whatever happens to next month's payment
prompt: A single photograph, one continuous scene, filling the whole frame. A South African parent in their forties standing at a kitchen counter in bright late-morning light, holding one of their child's used exercise books open in both hands and looking down at a page filled with handwriting. Four or five more used books are stacked on the counter beside them. No child in frame, no phone, no tablet. A quiet, satisfied expression - a parent seeing what has actually been done. Ordinary kitchen, real home, daylight through the window behind.
negative_prompt: any text, letters, numbers, words, signage, logos, watermarks, user-interface elements, phone screens showing apps, charts or graphs, cartoon, illustration, 3d render, cgi, airbrushed skin, plastic sheen, cinematic colour grade, film still look, motion blur, lens flare, extra fingers, malformed hands, distorted faces, stock-photo smiles, American classrooms, generic 'African' styling, collage, multiple panels, split screen, side-by-side frames, contact sheet, grid of images, storyboard, several phone mockups, device frames, app screenshots, before-and-after, picture-in-picture, borders, margins, framed print, lying down, slouching, idle scrolling, phone in bed, night-time bedroom, device floating in mid-air, phone standing on nothing, tablet balanced impossibly upright, no visible support, object hovering

_pipeline_only._note: NOT model input - read by the render script and the app.

framing.composition: subject in the lower two thirds, calm uncluttered space in the upper third where the slide's headline and caption sit - the image must never compete with the copy
framing.safe_area: keep the top 28% and bottom 18% visually quiet: the headline sits above, the button below

_revision_note: Adjusted 2026-07-30 alongside the student version: 'the teenager scrolling a phone' read as idling. Now they are showing the parent something specific, with a book open beside it.
_support_note: The device rests on something NAMED. 'Propped-up' describes the result, not the support, so the model rendered a phone standing upright on nothing (owner, 2026-07-30). A stack of exercise books or a cheap folding stand is both plausible in a South African home and something the model can actually draw in contact with the device.
_distinct_from_siblings: Rewritten 2026-07-30 alongside the student version: partner 01 and 03 were both a parent and teenager at a surface in the evening, and partner 06 is also the parent watching the child. This one is the parent ALONE in daylight with the child's finished books - different subject count, different time, no device - so the three parent slides no longer photograph the same moment.
